root_cause.text: The `ceph_decode_need()` bounds check in `osdmap_decode()` incorrectly accounted for only a single `sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` instead of `map->max_osd * sizeof(*map->osd_weight)`, causing insufficient validation and potential out-of-bounds memory access when decoding per-OSD weights.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains that the check "only accounts for sizeof(*map->osd_weight) once" while "both are decoded for each osd, i.e., map->max_osd times". The patch changes `sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` to `map->max_osd*sizeof(*map->osd_weight)` in the `ceph_decode_need()` call.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a bug in osdmap_decode where required buffer space for the osd_weight array was incorrectly calculated as a single element instead of the full array size.
intent_record.what: Changed the calculation of required buffer size in ceph_decode_need from sizeof(*map->osd_weight) to map->max_osd * sizeof(*map->osd_weight), multiplying by the number of OSDs.
intent_record.how: This ensures that the buffer size check accounts for the entire osd_weight array (size map->max_osd) instead of just a single entry, preventing potential out-of-bounds reads or processing of insufficient data.

vuln_statements.explanation: The bounds check using sizeof(*map->osd_weight) only accounts for a single element instead of the full array size map->max_osd * sizeof(*map->osd_weight), leading to insufficient validation and potential out-of-bounds access when decoding per-OSD weights.
